title: Your Phone System Is Probably Costing You More Than You Think
excerpt: Most small businesses are still hanging onto old phone infrastructure without realizing what they're leaving on the table — here's what's actually changing in 2026.

content.text: So I've been looking at what's happening in the business phone world right now, and there's this really interesting thing going on. Everyone's talking about upgrading to cloud-based systems — and I know that sounds like tech speak — but the real story underneath is that hanging onto traditional phone setups is becoming weirdly expensive in ways most owners don't even see coming.

Here's the thing: if you're still running a traditional phone system, you're probably dealing with POTS lines (Plain Old Telephone Service — basically the phone lines that have been around forever). They work fine, right? Except they're becoming harder to maintain, more expensive per line, and they're starting to disappear. Phone companies are actively phasing them out. So you've got this situation where the thing you're relying on is getting more fragile and more costly at the same time.
What's Really Happening Under the Hood

items: Telecom companies are sunsetting POTS lines — they're literally discontinuing this service because it's old infrastructure
Maintenance costs are climbing because your system needs parts that are harder to source
You're paying per line, per month, with no flexibility when your business grows or shrinks
You can't access your calls from anywhere — your phone lives at your desk or in your office

content.text: Most small business owners don't realize they're actually paying 30-50% more per line than they would with a cloud phone system, before you even factor in the installation, maintenance, and upgrade costs.

The cloud phone options available in 2026 aren't what they were five years ago. They've gotten way more stable, way more feature-rich, and honestly, way more necessary as businesses go hybrid or fully remote. You get your calls on your phone, your computer, wherever you are. You can add a line in minutes instead of days. And the cost per user is usually lower than what you're probably paying right now.

What's also interesting is that AI receptionists and answering services are actually becoming viable for small teams now. You don't need to hire someone to answer phones during business hours if you set up the right automation — and it actually sounds professional, not robotic.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Don't move just because cloud is trendy. But DO have a conversation with your IT person or a consultant about what your current system is actually costing you — all of it, including what you're paying in maintenance, the lines you're paying for but not using, and the productivity hit from people not being able to access calls remotely. Then compare that real number to what a cloud solution would actually run you. That math is almost always eye-opening, and it usually tips in favor of making a move sooner rather than later.

The deadline isn't today, but it is coming. The telecom companies aren't being shy about it. If you've been thinking about this, now's actually the time to get serious about it instead of waiting for the decision to get made for you.
